_doc: What people are actually shopping for, by month. Pinterest is a search engine and its users plan ahead, so the window OPENS about 3-6 weeks before the event and closes hard the day after. Pinning dorm content on 2 September is pinning into a search term that collapsed in mid-August. Keep this file current - it is data, not code.
_lead_time_doc: Pinterest searches run ahead of purchase. Treat the month entry as 'what to pin NOW', not 'what is happening now'.
_retired_doc: A theme past its month is actively harmful: it consumes pin slots and lands on a search term nobody is typing. Use SINGLE TOKENS ('dorm', not 'dorm room') — products are titled 'for Dorm & College', so a two-word key never matches and the demotion silently does nothing.
_off_niche_doc: Golden Home Project is home organization. Kids' character bottles, bento boxes and TV wall mounts drifted into the vetted pool and were consuming pin slots on 2026-09-02. Blocked from pinning; they stay in the catalogue for other uses. Extended 2026-09-14: drinkware and stadium seating were still publishing from queue entries created before the block existed; the block is now applied at POSTING time as well as generation.
_seasonal_doc: Halloween and Christmas were absent entirely until 2026-09-13. Pinterest reports Halloween search peaking July-October and holiday planning starting in September, so both windows were being entered after they had already opened. Sourced from Amazon's Seasonal Decor best-seller node (13679381), which rotates its own inventory with the calendar.
